vulns.description: Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them.   An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer.  Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them.   An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer.  Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

### Impact A maliciously crafted DNS message may cause dns.name.from_wire_parser() to use excessive CPU for DNS name decompression.  Applications that process untrusted DNS wire form messages with dnspython may be degraded or DoS'd by the extra CPU use required.  ### Patches This problem is fixed in dnspython 2.9.0.  ### Workarounds There are no known workarounds.  ### Credit Evgenios Gkritsis, Department of Informatics, University of Piraeus & Athena Research Center, Greece Constantinos Patsakis, Department of Informatics, University of Piraeus & Athena Research Center, Greece George Stergiopoulos, Department of Informatics, Athens University of Economics and Business, Greece
